title: Straight-Line Graphs
description: Explore the gradient, y-intercept and equation $y=mx+c$, then use them to plot straight lines and identify parallel and perpendicular lines.

notes.heading: Plotting Points on a Grid

illustration.alt: A straight line drawn on a coordinate grid, showing the y-intercept, a gradient triangle and the equation y equals mx plus c.
illustration.caption: A straight line is fixed by its gradient and y-intercept.

notes.body:
📌 Definition
A coordinate grid is made from a horizontal $x$-axis and a vertical $y$-axis that cross at the origin $(0,0)$. Every point is written as an ordered pair $(x,y)$.

🔑 Key Concept
To plot a point, move horizontally first (positive is right, negative is left), then vertically (positive is up, negative is down).

💡 Worked Example
Plot $A(3,2)$, $B(-2,4)$, $C(-1,-3)$ and $D(2,-2)$.
• $A$ is 3 right and 2 up.
• $B$ is 2 left and 4 up.
• $C$ is 1 left and 3 down.
• $D$ is 2 right and 2 down.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Always write coordinates as $(x,y)$; order matters.
• Points on the $x$-axis have $y=0$.
• Points on the $y$-axis have $x=0$.

✅ Check
Count from the origin along the $x$-axis, then move parallel to the $y$-axis.

notes.heading: Gradient of a Straight Line
notes.body:
📌 Definition
The gradient $m$ measures how steep a straight line is. For two points $(x_1,y_1)$ and $(x_2,y_2)$:
$$m = \dfrac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}$$

🔑 How it works
• A positive gradient slopes upwards from left to right.
• A negative gradient slopes downwards from left to right.
• A zero gradient is horizontal.
• A vertical line has an undefined gradient.

💡 Worked Example
Find the gradient through $A(1,2)$ and $B(5,10)$.
$$m = \dfrac{10 - 2}{5 - 1} = \dfrac{8}{4} = 2$$
For every 1 unit to the right, the line rises 2 units.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Mixing the order of the points. If you subtract $y_1 - y_2$ in the numerator, you must subtract $x_1 - x_2$ in the denominator.

notes.heading: The Equation $y = mx + c$
notes.body:
📌 Definition
The equation of a non-vertical straight line can be written as:
$$y = mx + c$$
where $m$ is the gradient and $c$ is the $y$-intercept, the value of $y$ where the line crosses the $y$-axis.

🔑 How it works
• $m$ tells you the steepness and direction of the line.
• $c$ tells you where the line hits the $y$-axis at the point $(0,c)$.

💡 Worked Example
For $y = 3x - 2$:
• $m = 3$, so the line rises 3 units for every 1 unit to the right.
• $c = -2$, so the line crosses the $y$-axis at $(0,-2)$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• The equation must have $y$ as the subject before you read $m$ and $c$.
• Lines with the same $m$ are parallel.
• Lines with the same $c$ cross the $y$-axis at the same point.

notes.heading: Plotting from $y = mx + c$
notes.body:
🔑 How it works
1. Mark the $y$-intercept $(0,c)$.
2. From that point, use the gradient to locate a second point: move 1 unit right and $m$ units up (or down if $m$ is negative).
3. Join the points with a straight line and extend it in both directions.

💡 Worked Example
Plot $y = 2x + 1$.
• The $y$-intercept is $(0,1)$.
• The gradient is $2$, so move 1 right and 2 up to $(1,3)$.
• Draw a straight line through $(0,1)$ and $(1,3)$.

💡 Worked Example
Plot $y = -\dfrac{1}{2}x + 4$.
• The $y$-intercept is $(0,4)$.
• The gradient is $-\dfrac{1}{2}$, so move 2 right and 1 down to $(2,3)$.
• Draw a straight line through the two points.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Swapping rise and run. A gradient of $\dfrac{2}{3}$ means move 3 right then 2 up, not 2 right then 3 up.

notes.heading: Finding the Equation of a Line
notes.body:
📌 Key Concept
If you know the gradient $m$ and one point $(x_1,y_1)$, you can use point-slope form:
$$y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)$$
Then rearrange to $y = mx + c$.

If you know two points, first find the gradient, then substitute one point to find $c$.

💡 Worked Example 1
Find the equation of the line with gradient $2$ passing through $(3,7)$.
$$y - 7 = 2(x - 3)$$
$$y - 7 = 2x - 6$$
$$y = 2x + 1$$

💡 Worked Example 2
Find the equation of the line through $(1,4)$ and $(3,10)$.
Step 1: gradient.
$$m = \dfrac{10 - 4}{3 - 1} = \dfrac{6}{2} = 3$$
Step 2: substitute $(1,4)$ into $y = 3x + c$.
$$4 = 3(1) + c \Rightarrow c = 1$$
Step 3: equation.
$$y = 3x + 1$$

✅ Check
Substitute the other point: $10 = 3(3) + 1 = 10$. Correct.

notes.heading: Parallel and Perpendicular Lines
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Two lines are parallel if they never meet. They have the same gradient:
$$m_1 = m_2$$
Two lines are perpendicular if they meet at a right angle. Their gradients multiply to $-1$:
$$m_1 \times m_2 = -1$$
So the perpendicular gradient is the negative reciprocal $-\dfrac{1}{m}$.

🔑 How it works
If a line has gradient $m$:
• a parallel line also has gradient $m$;
• a perpendicular line has gradient $-\dfrac{1}{m}$.

💡 Worked Example
For $y = 4x + 1$:
• a parallel line is $y = 4x - 3$;
• a perpendicular line is $y = -\dfrac{1}{4}x + 5$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Thinking perpendicular gradients are just negatives of each other. The negative reciprocal of $4$ is $-\dfrac{1}{4}$, not $-4$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Parallel lines share a gradient but have different $y$-intercepts (otherwise they are the same line).
• Horizontal lines are perpendicular to vertical lines.

notes.heading: Horizontal and Vertical Lines
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A horizontal line has equation $y = c$ and gradient $0$.
A vertical line has equation $x = a$ and an undefined gradient.

🔑 How it works
For $y = c$, every point on the line has the same $y$-coordinate, so the change in $y$ is zero.
For $x = a$, every point has the same $x$-coordinate, so the change in $x$ is zero and the gradient formula divides by zero.

💡 Worked Example
Write the equation of:
1. The horizontal line through $(4,-3)$: $y = -3$.
2. The vertical line through $(4,-3)$: $x = 4$.
The two lines cross at $(4,-3)$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Horizontal lines are parallel to the $x$-axis.
• Vertical lines are parallel to the $y$-axis.
• The form $y = mx + c$ cannot describe a vertical line.

flashcards.definition: A measure of how steep a straight line is, equal to the change in $y$ divided by the change in $x$.
The value of $y$ where a line crosses the $y$-axis; the constant $c$ in $y=mx+c$.
$y=mx+c$, where $m$ is the gradient and $c$ is the $y$-intercept.
Mark the $y$-intercept, then use the gradient to find a second point and draw the line.
flashcards.example: For $y=3x+2$, mark $(0,2)$ and move 1 right, 3 up to $(1,5)$.

flashcards.definition: Lines that never meet; they have equal gradients.
Lines that meet at a right angle; the product of their gradients is $-1$.
A line with equation $y=c$ and gradient $0$.
flashcards.example: $y=-2$ is a horizontal line through every point with $y$-coordinate $-2$.

flashcards.definition: A line with equation $x=a$; its gradient is undefined.
flashcards.example: $x=5$ is a vertical line through every point with $x$-coordinate $5$.

flashcards.definition: The value of $x$ where a line crosses the $x$-axis, found by setting $y=0$.
flashcards.example: For $y=2x-6$, setting $y=0$ gives $x=3$, so the $x$-intercept is $(3,0)$.

flashcards.definition: $y-y_1=m(x-x_1)$, used when the gradient and one point are known.
A gradient that cannot be calculated because the change in $x$ is zero.
flashcards.example: The vertical line $x=4$ has an undefined gradient.

questions.stem: What is the gradient of the line through $(2,3)$ and $(6,11)$?

questions.explanation: In $y=mx+c$, the $y$-intercept is $c=-3$, so the line crosses the $y$-axis at $(0,-3)$.

questions.stem: Which equation represents a line with gradient $-2$ and $y$-intercept $4$?
Find the equation of the line with gradient $3$ passing through $(0,2)$.
questions.explanation: The $y$-intercept is $2$ and the gradient is $3$, so the equation is $y=3x+2$.

questions.stem: Find the equation of the line through $(1,5)$ and $(3,9)$.
questions.explanation: The gradient is $\dfrac{9-5}{3-1}=2$. Substituting $(1,5)$ gives $5=2+c$, so $c=3$ and $y=2x+3$.
Parallel lines have equal gradients, so the answer must keep $m=\dfrac{3}{4}$.

questions.stem: A line is perpendicular to $y=2x+5$. What is its gradient?
What is the equation of the horizontal line through $(7,-3)$?
questions.explanation: A horizontal line has equation $y=c$, so through $(7,-3)$ the equation is $y=-3$.

questions.stem: The line through $(0,c)$ and $(3,10)$ has gradient $2$. Find $c$.
Which point lies on the line $y=3x-1$?
questions.explanation: Substituting $x=1$ gives $y=3(1)-1=2$, so $(1,2)$ lies on the line.

questions.stem: Find the equation of the line through $(-1,4)$ that is parallel to $y=3x+2$.
questions.explanation: Parallel means $m=3$. Substituting $(-1,4)$ gives $4=-3+c$, so $c=7$ and $y=3x+7$.

questions.stem: The points $(2,a)$ and $(6,5)$ lie on a line with gradient $-\dfrac{1}{2}$. Find $a$.

questions.explanation: The negative reciprocal of $\dfrac{2}{3}$ is $-\dfrac{3}{2}$, so $y=-\dfrac{3}{2}x+1$ is perpendicular.

questions.stem: A taxi charges a fixed fee of $5 plus $2 per kilometre. Which equation gives the cost $C$ for $k$ kilometres?
questions.explanation: The fixed $5 is the $y$-intercept and the $2 per kilometre is the gradient, so $C=2k+5$.
